note: Animated fact graphics (fx), remotion/src/Fx.tsx and remotion/src/fx/: the templates, the two placements and the design preview (FxPreview, scripts/render_fx_preview.py, which also reads the preview timing and samples from here). Pixel values in placements are output pixels (1080x1920); in templates they are design pixels at content scale 1, scaled into the placement's box. Times in templates are seconds from the template's start; each template's whole animation must be still by its durationS (checked at render).

popout.note: The card: widthRatio of the frame's width, `height` tall, centred on x and on centerY. It jumps out of the TV (from out.fromScale of the face, squashed to its shape), the room behind it (background and TV, not the host or the captions) dims by dim.opacity as it lifts, and it flies back in at the end.

safe.note: The settled card (its tilt included, not its shadow) must stay inside these: topPx below the platform's top bar, sideMarginPx in from both edges (the cover's margin), and captionClearancePx above the caption block at captionMaxLines lines (CAPTIONS in Captions.tsx), which also keeps it clear of the host's eyes below the captions. captionMaxLines is 1: the card reaches below the top of a two-line caption, so while it is out the captions must stay on one line (scripts/captions.py max_lines is 2; the wiring pass has to cap it, channel docs/fx.md).

reel.note: Fx in a reel (reelline/media/fx, scripts/render_reel.py): a paragraph's @fx card (paragraph 1's: `opening`) starts on its anchor word (else the paragraph's first word) and stays out for placements.popout.leadS + the template's durationS + holdS, then flies back (back.durationS). It is cut short to end gapS before the next card and outroGapS before the end card; one that would then hold less than minHoldS after settling is left out. Captions stay on one line from captionPadS before a card starts to captionPadS after it ends. maxPerReel and minPerScript: the parser's cap and punch-up's minimum (prompts/punchup.md); consecutive: cards allowed on paragraphs in a row; beforeTag: a card allowed on the paragraph before the tag (the closing jab); queue: a card that would start within gapS of the one before it waits for it (from gapS after its end, at most queueLagS after its own paragraph ends) instead of being left out (reelline/media/fx planned()). These values are the classic style's: the straight style (host/style.py STYLE_MODE) lays its own over them (Style.fx_reel: 3-7 cards, gapS 0.3, consecutive, beforeTag and queue on, queueLagS 1.5). Its sound: host/sfx/config.py FX_POP.

opening.note: Paragraph 1's @fx card is the frame-0 card (reelline/media/fx planned(), the event's frame0): with fromFrame0 on it is out from frame 0, whatever its anchor, already settled (the card in its box, the room dimmed, the template at its end, so the fact reads on the first frame and in the platforms' 1.5 s cover frame). Its only motion is the settle: the card from settle.fromScale to 1 over settle.durationS. It holds at least minHoldS, or as long as a card on its first word would (back by paragraph 2's first word), whichever is later, then flies back as usual (placements.popout.back); a card after it too close for gapS is left out, never this one. No TV click (it doesn't spring out). Off: paragraph 1's card plays like any other.

counter.note: The optional days-left tag: daysLeft counts from the reel's publish date (its slot date), never the render date (channel docs/fx.md).
counter.label: days left

abroad.note: Georgia (origin: the map, a dot on `from`, its name under the map, or over it when the flight heads down more steeply than labelAboveSin) and the destination (a pin, its name over or under it, whichever lands nearer) on a line the way the destination lies from `from` on a world map (remotion/src/fx/destinations.json; one not listed there flies at unknownDeg, counterclockwise from east: up and to the left). The pin is at least layout.flightGapPx clear of Georgia and layout.minFlightPx from `from`; the plane flies an arc bowed by arc.liftRatio of the flight's length (its control point) and stops plane.clearPx short of the pin. The name shrinks to fit dest.maxLabelWidthPx; a name of two or more words that would shrink below dest.wrapBelowPx on one line goes onto two (split where its wider line is narrowest) when that's bigger. Layout: layout.ts abroadLayout.

apply.note: A browser window window.width wide; the address bar spans it (address.marginPx in from each side) and the domain is as big as fits it (at most address.textPx); the go button sits on the page under the bar, at the right, with placeholder lines beside it.

steps.note: 2-4 numbered circles top to bottom, each label to the right of its circle, all labels at one size: the largest from labelPx down (to labelMinPx) at which the list fits the card's content box at the placement's full scale, every label on one line; only when even labelMinPx doesn't fit that way does a label of two or more words go onto two lines (layout.ts stepsLayout). Circles list.rRatio of the label size (list.rMin..rMax), the line between two at least list.minLinePx, stretched up to maxLinePx to fill the box's height; each label labelGapPx right of its circle, neighbouring labels rowGapPx apart; numbers numberRatio of the radius.

preview.note: FxPreview: the real scene (background, TV, chair, the host idling with the rest mouth, a sample caption) and one sample in one placement. The fx runs from fxStartS to fxEndS; stills: start (startAfterS[placement] after fxStartS: the transition in), mid (midS[sample] seconds after the template's start, a moment with motion in it), settled (settledAfterS after the template's durationS).
